questions.q: Diethyl adipate (diethyl hexanedioate) is treated with sodium ethoxide in ethanol, followed by dilute acid. The product is:
questions.explain: C-2 attacks C-6 intramolecularly, closing a five-membered ring and expelling ethoxide to give the cyclic β-keto ester. Cyclopentanone forms only after hydrolysis and heating.

questions.q: Diethyl pimelate (diethyl heptanedioate) is treated with (i) NaOEt, (ii) H₃O⁺, (iii) heat. The final product is:
questions.explain: C-2 attacks C-7, so a six-membered β-keto ester forms; hydrolysis gives the β-keto acid, which loses CO₂ on heating to cyclohexanone.

questions.q: Which base is NOT suitable for carrying out a Dieckmann condensation of diethyl adipate?
options: An alkoxide base in a dry alcohol
questions.explain: Aqueous NaOH hydrolyses the ester groups instead of forming the ester enolate; an alkoxide or NaH is used, as in the Claisen condensation.

questions.q: Diethyl adipate is treated with (i) NaOEt; (ii) CH₃I; (iii) H₃O⁺, heat. The final product is:
questions.explain: The Dieckmann β-keto ester is methylated at the acidic carbon between its two carbonyls (C-1, next to the ring C=O); hydrolysis and loss of CO₂ then leave the methyl α to the ketone.
